$comment: FR-DX-01 allowlist: public members that are genuinely demonstrated by the samples but invisible in compiled IL/metadata, or that cannot appear there at all. Every entry needs a one-line reason; prefer closing a gap with a real sample demonstration over adding an entry. The gate fails on stale entries (member gone, or now demonstrated).

entries.reason: Static holder whose only public member is the ActivitySourceName const; const use IL-inlines the literal, so no sample reference to the type can ever appear in metadata.
Const-only profile-identifier holder; sample 10 uses Profiles.DidCommV2 et al., but consts IL-inline so the type leaves no metadata reference.
Const-only protocol-URI holder; the cookbook's Empty sections use its MessageType/ProtocolUri consts, which IL-inline.
Const-only routing-URI holder; sample 04 uses ForwardConstants.PayloadMediaType, which IL-inlines.
Const-only trace-protocol holder; sample 07 uses Trace.HeaderName/ReportUriField, which IL-inline.
Library-constructed result record; samples read every property but honest sample code never fabricates a pack result. Public only because it is the record's primary constructor.

Library-constructed result record (14-arg primary ctor); a sample constructing one would fabricate verification evidence. Arguably could be non-public, but records require a public primary ctor for their value semantics.
Library-constructed result record; SendAsync is the only honest producer, and samples read every property.
Library-constructed result record; ForwardProcessor.ProcessAsync is the only honest producer (sample 04 reads every property).
Library-constructed dispatch result; samples read Result/Reply/Handler but fabricating an outcome in a sample would be dishonest. Candidate for internal ctor in a future major.
FromUnpackResult is the supported construction path (demonstrated in sample 07); the positional ctor exists as the record's primary ctor and deliberately cannot assert RecipientAddressing (#61).
Raised by the WebSocket transport; consumers subscribe and read (demonstrated in the cookbook and sample 05) — constructing the args in a sample would fake a lifecycle event.
